notes.en: four (before a counter: 네 명, 네 시)
notes.explain: 숫자 4는 ‘넷’이에요. 그런데 개, 명, 시 같은 단위 앞에서는 ‘네’로 바뀌어요. ‘네’(yes)와 소리가 같아요.
notes.explain_en: The plain number four is 넷. Before counters like 개, 명 and 시 it changes to 네. It sounds the same as 네 (yes).

examples.en: There are four people in my family.
Let's meet at four.
Four coffees, please.
There are four bottles of water in the fridge.

examples.ko: 고양이가 네 마리 있어요. 모두 귀여워요.
examples.en: I have four cats. They are all cute.

notes.explain: ‘제일’은 한자 第一(number one)에서 왔어요. 그래서 ‘제일 좋아요’는 ‘1등으로 좋아요’라는 느낌이에요.
notes.explain_en: 제일 comes from the Chinese characters 第一, 'number one'. So 제일 좋아요 feels like 'ranked first in how good'.
notes.usage: 제일 = most / first (speech). 가장 means the same in writing.

notes.explain: 한국 여름에는 ‘장마’라고 하는 비가 많이 오는 때가 있어요. 해마다 조금씩 달라요.
notes.explain_en: Korean summers have a rainy season called 장마. The timing is a little different every year.

notes.explain_en: Autumn has 추석 (Chuseok), a big Korean holiday. It usually falls in September or October.

notes.explain_en: Many families do 김장 before winter: they make a huge batch of kimchi to eat through the cold months.

notes.explain: ‘이따가’는 오늘 조금 뒤예요. ‘나중에’는 언제인지 몰라요. 며칠 뒤나 몇 년 뒤도 ‘나중에’예요.
notes.explain_en: 이따가 means a bit later today. 나중에 is an unspecified later time, from a few days to several years.

examples.en: Come again later.
I'll do my homework later.
Shall we eat together sometime later?
I'm busy now. Let's talk later.
Someday I want to work in Korea.

notes.explain: 요일 이름은 한자 뜻으로 기억하면 쉬워요. 월(달), 화(불), 수(물), 목(나무), 금(쇠), 토(흙), 일(해)이에요.
notes.explain_en: The day names are easy to remember through the meaning of their Chinese characters: 월 (moon), 화 (fire), 수 (water), 목 (wood), 금 (metal), 토 (earth), 일 (sun).

examples.en: My little sibling knows all the days of the week.
At this restaurant the menu changes every day of the week.
What day of the week is the class?
I write the exam date and the day of the week.
My younger sibling doesn't know the names of the days yet.

notes.explain: ‘버스를 타요’처럼 ‘을/를’을 써요. 자전거, 스키, 말도 모두 ‘타다’예요.
notes.explain_en: Use 을/를 with 타다: 버스를 타요. Bikes, skis and horses also use 타다.

examples.en: I took a taxi to the airport.
I was on the plane for twelve hours.
I go to the office by subway.
I want to ride a bike by the Han River this weekend.
How do you get there? — I take the bus.

notes.explain: 지하철 안내판에는 ‘환승’이라고 쓰여 있어요. 말할 때는 ‘갈아타다’를 많이 써요.
notes.explain_en: Subway signs say 환승 (transfer). In speech people mostly say 갈아타다.

examples.en: I transfer from the subway to the bus.
I transferred to Line 2 at City Hall.
Where shall we transfer? — We transfer at Seoul Station.
I transfer twice by subway to get to work.
I changed buses and went home.

notes.explain: ‘말다’는 혼자 거의 안 써요. ‘-지 마세요’처럼 동사 뒤에 붙어요. 친구에게는 ‘-지 마’라고 해요.
notes.explain_en: 말다 hardly ever stands alone. It comes after a verb as in -지 마세요. To a friend, just say -지 마.

examples.en: Don't worry too much.
Don't sleep during class.
Please don't make phone calls in the library.
Please don't tell this story to your friend.
Please don't drink coffee at night.

notes.explain_en: Getting off uses 에서 (버스에서 내려요), but getting on uses 를 (버스를 타요). The particles are different.

examples.en: I'm going to get off at the next station.
It's raining outside.

notes.explain: ‘알다’는 ㄹ 동사예요. ‘압니다’, ‘아세요’처럼 ㄹ이 없어져요. ‘알아요’는 그대로 써요.
notes.explain_en: 알다 is an ㄹ verb: the ㄹ drops before ㅂ and ㅅ, as in 압니다 and 아세요. But 알아요 keeps it.

phrases.example: 저 사람 마음은 알다가도 모르겠어요.
phrases.literal: “I seem to know, yet I don't”
phrases.en_equiv: I just can't figure it out
phrases.meaning_en: Used when someone or something stays a puzzle even though you thought you understood.

examples.en: Do you know that person's phone number?
I know a lot of Korean songs.
I know that person well.
Do you know this way? — No, I don't.

examples.ko: 저는 그 가게를 알아요. 음식이 맛있어요.
examples.en: I know that shop. The food is good.

notes.explain: ‘죄송해요’는 ‘미안해요’보다 더 공손해요. 손님, 어른, 회사 사람에게는 ‘죄송해요’를 쓰고 친구에게는 ‘미안해’라고 해요.
notes.explain_en: 죄송해요 is more polite than 미안해요. Use it with customers, elders and colleagues, and 미안해 with friends.

examples.en: I'm really sorry for being late to the meeting.
I feel so guilty toward my parents.
I'm sorry. I can't go right now.
I'm sorry. We have no seats today.
Oh, I'm sorry! Does it hurt a lot?

notes.explain: ‘고프다’는 거의 ‘배가 고파요’로만 써요. ‘으’가 없어지고 ‘고파요’가 돼요. 한 단어로 ‘배고파요’라고도 써요.
notes.explain_en: 고프다 is almost only used as 배가 고파요. The 으 drops, giving 고파요. It is also written as one word: 배고파요.

phrases.example: 배가 고파서 배가 등에 붙겠어요.
phrases.en_equiv: so hungry my stomach is empty
phrases.meaning_en: A humorous way to say you are extremely hungry.

examples.en: I skipped breakfast. I'm hungry.
I'm hungry already.
Are you hungry? Shall we eat together?

examples.ko: 어제는 배가 많이 고팠어요. 밤에 라면을 먹었어요.
examples.en: I was very hungry yesterday. I ate ramyeon at night.
I'm not hungry yet.

notes.explain: ‘가장 + 형용사’는 most예요. 그런데 ‘가장’에는 family head라는 다른 뜻도 있어요. 문장에서 구분해요.
notes.explain_en: 가장 + adjective means 'most'. The same sound can also mean 'head of a household', so check the sentence.
notes.usage: 가장 = most (written/formal). 제일 = most (common in speech).

examples.en: This shop's cake is the most delicious.
This building is the tallest in Seoul.
I'm the youngest at my company.
Today is the coldest day this week.
The hospital is the closest one around here.

notes.explain: “잘못”은 동사 바로 앞에 와요. 하는 일이 틀렸다는 뜻이에요. 그리고 “잘못했어요”는 “내가 틀렸어요, 미안해요”라는 사과예요.
notes.explain_en: 잘못 goes right before the verb and means the action went wrong. Also, 잘못했어요 on its own is an apology: "I was wrong, I'm sorry."

phrases.example: 죄송합니다, 전화를 잘못 걸었어요.
phrases.meaning_en: What you say when you reach the wrong person by phone.

examples.en: I misheard.
I took the wrong bus.
I pressed the wrong phone number.
I wrote my friend's name wrong.
A package came to me by mistake.

notes.explain: ‘특히’는 앞에서 말한 것 중 하나를 뽑아서 강조할 때 써요. 그래서 보통 두 번째 문장에 와요.
notes.explain_en: 특히 picks out one thing from what you just said and stresses it. That's why it usually starts the second sentence.

examples.ko: 저는 한국 음식을 좋아해요. 특히 김치찌개를 좋아해요.
examples.en: I like Korean food, especially kimchi stew.

examples.ko: 저는 과일을 좋아해요. 특히 딸기가 좋아요.
examples.en: I like fruit, especially strawberries.

examples.ko: 여름은 더워요. 특히 팔월에는 아주 더워요.
examples.en: Summer is hot. Especially in August it's very hot.

examples.ko: 서울은 사람이 많아요. 특히 주말에는 지하철에 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Seoul has a lot of people. Especially on weekends, the subway is crowded.

examples.ko: 한국어 공부가 재미있어요. 특히 발음 연습이 재미있어요.
examples.en: Studying Korean is fun. Pronunciation practice in particular is fun.

notes.explain: “어떤”은 꼭 명사 앞에 와요: 어떤 색, 어떤 사람. 혼자 쓰지 않아요. “어때요?”와 달라요.
notes.explain_en: 어떤 always comes right before a noun: 어떤 색, 어떤 사람. It can't stand alone, and it is different from 어때요?.

phrases.example: 실례지만, 어떤 일을 하세요?
phrases.literal: “what kind of work do you do?”
phrases.en_equiv: What do you do for a living?
phrases.meaning_en: A polite way to ask someone's job.

examples.en: What kind of food do you like?
What kind of movie did you see?
What color do you like? — I like blue.
What kind of exercise do you do on weekends?
What kind of person came?

notes.explain: 보통은 그냥 “배우”라고 말해요. 영화에 나오면 영화배우, 드라마에 나오면 드라마 배우라고 구분할 수 있어요.
notes.explain_en: People usually just say 배우 (actor). If you want to be specific, an actor in films is a 영화배우 and one in dramas is a 드라마 배우.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 얼굴이 영화배우 뺨쳐요.
phrases.en_equiv: to rival a movie star (in looks)

examples.en: That film actor appears in American movies too.
I've seen all of this actor's films.
A movie actor acts in films.

examples.ko: 영화배우가 되고 싶어요. 연기를 배울 거예요.
examples.en: I want to become a movie actor. I'm going to learn acting.

examples.ko: 저 영화배우를 알아요? — 네, 아주 유명해요.
examples.en: Do you know that movie star? — Yes, he's very famous.

more.en: That film actor appears in American movies too.
I've seen all of this actor's films.
A movie actor acts in films.

more.ko: 영화배우가 되고 싶어요. 연기를 배울 거예요.
more.en: I want to become a movie actor. I'm going to learn acting.

more.ko: 저 영화배우를 알아요? — 네, 아주 유명해요.
more.en: Do you know that movie star? — Yes, he's very famous.

notes.explain: “말레이시아”와 “인도네시아”는 이름이 비슷해서 헷갈려요. “말레이”로 시작하면 말레이시아, “인도네”로 시작하면 인도네시아예요.
notes.explain_en: 말레이시아 and 인도네시아 look alike and are easy to mix up. If it starts with 말레이 it is Malaysia; if it starts with 인도네 it is Indonesia.

examples.en: Malaysia is hot all year round.
I have a friend from Malaysia.
It rains often in Malaysia.
There is a Malaysian restaurant in our neighborhood.
I met a friend in Malaysia during vacation.

more.en: Malaysia is hot all year round.
I have a friend from Malaysia.
It rains often in Malaysia.
There is a Malaysian restaurant in our neighborhood.
I met a friend in Malaysia during vacation.

notes.explain: “카나다”가 아니라 “캐나다”라고 써요. 첫 글자는 “캐”예요. 발음도 [캐나다]예요.
notes.explain_en: It is written 캐나다, not 카나다. The first letter is 캐, and you say it that way too.

examples.en: Winters in Canada are very cold.
My friend is from Canada.
Canada is very far from Korea.
What is Canada like? — It's very big.
I'm going to go to Canada in the summer.

more.en: Winters in Canada are very cold.
My friend is from Canada.
Canada is very far from Korea.
What is Canada like? — It's very big.
I'm going to go to Canada in the summer.

notes.explain: 이름이 길어서 뉴스에서는 “인니”라고 줄여서 쓰기도 해요. 보통 말할 때는 “인도네시아”라고 해요.
notes.explain_en: The name is long, so news and online text sometimes shorten it to 인니. In normal speech you say 인도네시아.

examples.en: Indonesia has a lot of islands.
I want to go to Bali in Indonesia.
My Indonesian friend likes Korean songs.
I worked in Indonesia last year.

examples.ko: 인도네시아는 어디에 있어요? — 말레이시아 옆에 있어요.
examples.en: Where is Indonesia? — It is next to Malaysia.

more.en: Indonesia has a lot of islands.
I want to go to Bali in Indonesia.
My Indonesian friend likes Korean songs.
I worked in Indonesia last year.

more.ko: 인도네시아는 어디에 있어요? — 말레이시아 옆에 있어요.
more.en: Where is Indonesia? — It is next to Malaysia.

notes.explain: “로시아”가 아니라 “러시아”예요. 첫 글자가 “러”예요. 러시아 말은 “러시아어”예요.
notes.explain_en: It is 러시아, not 로시아. The first letter is 러. The language is 러시아어.

examples.en: Russian winters are really long and cold.
Russia is the biggest country in the world.
Russia is a very big country.
My Russian friend likes kimchi.
I want to go to Russia in winter.

more.en: Russian winters are really long and cold.
Russia is the biggest country in the world.
Russia is a very big country.
My Russian friend likes kimchi.
I want to go to Russia in winter.

notes.explain: 예전에는 “몽고”라고도 썼어요. 지금은 “몽골”이라고 써요. 오래된 책이나 말에서 “몽고”가 나오기도 해요.
notes.explain_en: It used to be written 몽고 in Korean too. Today you write 몽골. You may still see 몽고 in older books or hear it in older speech.

examples.en: Mongolians are good at riding horses.
Mongolia has more horses than people.
My Mongolian friend works at a company in Seoul.
The sky in Mongolia is really beautiful.
A friend is coming from Mongolia next month.

more.en: Mongolians are good at riding horses.
Mongolia has more horses than people.
My Mongolian friend works at a company in Seoul.
The sky in Mongolia is really beautiful.
A friend is coming from Mongolia next month.

notes.explain: 한국어로는 “비엣남”이 아니라 “베트남”이에요. 처음 소리가 “베”예요. 쌀국수 가게도 “베트남 쌀국수”라고 많이 써요.
notes.explain_en: In Korean it is 베트남, not 비엣남. It starts with the sound 베. Noodle shops often put 베트남 in the name too: 베트남 쌀국수.

examples.en: In Vietnam, people often eat noodles for breakfast.
Vietnamese coffee is very sweet.
I want to eat Vietnamese rice noodles.
A friend came to Korea from Vietnam.
I'm going to meet my Vietnamese friend tomorrow.

more.en: In Vietnam, people often eat noodles for breakfast.
Vietnamese coffee is very sweet.
I want to eat Vietnamese rice noodles.
A friend came to Korea from Vietnam.
I'm going to meet my Vietnamese friend tomorrow.

notes.explain: 나라 이름 뒤에 “어”를 붙이면 그 나라 말이 돼요. 프랑스어, 중국어, 일본어가 그래요. 영어만 조금 달라요.
notes.explain_en: Add 어 after a country name to get its language: 프랑스어, 중국어, 일본어. English is the odd one out: 영어, not 영국어.

examples.en: Paris is in France.
I like French films.
I'm meeting my French friend in Paris.
France is famous for its bread.
I'm going to France this year.

more.en: Paris is in France.
I like French films.
I'm meeting my French friend in Paris.
France is famous for its bread.
I'm going to France this year.

notes.explain: ‘다리’는 bridge도 되고 leg도 돼요. ‘다리를 건너요’는 bridge, ‘다리가 아파요’는 leg예요.
notes.explain_en: 다리 can be a bridge or a leg. 다리를 건너요 is a bridge and 다리가 아파요 is a leg.

phrases.example: 돌다리도 두들겨 보고 건너라고 하니까 계약서를 다시 읽을게요.
phrases.literal: “even a stone bridge, tap it before crossing”
phrases.meaning_en: A proverb telling you to be careful even when something seems safe.

phrases.example: 친구가 저하고 사장님 사이에 다리를 놓아 줬어요.
phrases.meaning_en: To connect two people or sides, for example by introducing them.

examples.en: Cross this bridge.
The Han River bridges are beautiful at night.
Shall we take a photo on the bridge?
There is a small park under the bridge.
There are many bridges over the Han River.

notes.explain: 버스는 ‘정류장’, 지하철은 ‘역’이라고 해요. 정류장 이름은 보통 가까운 건물이나 장소 이름이에요.
notes.explain_en: A bus stops at a 정류장 and the subway at a 역. Stop names are usually the nearby building or place.

examples.en: The bus stop is in front of my house.
I wait for the bus at the stop.
Is there a bus stop near here?
It takes five minutes from the bus stop to my office.
The next stop is City Hall.

notes.explain: 배는 “타다”와 같이 써요: 배를 타요, 배에서 내려요. 지하철이나 버스와 같아요.
notes.explain_en: Boats go with 타다: 배를 타요 (ride a boat), 배에서 내려요 (get off). Just like buses and subways.
notes.usage: 배 = boat/ship. Also 배 = stomach (배가 아파요), and 배 = pear.

phrases.example: 우리는 한배를 탔어요.
phrases.en_equiv: to be in the same boat
phrases.meaning_en: To share the same fate or risk with others.

phrases.example: 의견이 많아서 배가 산으로 가요.
phrases.en_equiv: too many cooks spoil the broth
phrases.meaning_en: Used when too many opinions send a project in the wrong direction.

examples.en: I took a boat out on the sea.
I looked at the sea from the deck of the ship.
I go to the island by boat.

examples.ko: 배가 아주 커요. 사람이 많이 타요.
examples.en: The ship is huge. Many people ride it.
The ship leaves the port at ten.

notes.explain: ‘음식’은 먹는 것 전체예요. ‘요리’는 만드는 일이나 만든 음식이에요. ‘중국 요리’, ‘한국 요리’처럼 나라 이름과 같이 써요.
notes.explain_en: 음식 is food in general. 요리 is the act of cooking or a prepared dish, often with a country name: 중국 요리, 한국 요리.

examples.en: I like Korean cooking.
My husband is a good cook.

examples.ko: 저녁에 요리를 할 거예요. 뭐 먹고 싶어요?
examples.en: I'm going to cook this evening. What do you want to eat?
What is today's special dish?

examples.ko: 일요일에는 형이 요리를 하고 제가 청소를 해요.
examples.en: On Sundays my older brother cooks and I clean.

notes.explain: ‘소갈비’는 소고기 갈비, ‘돼지갈비’는 돼지고기 갈비예요. 국물이 있는 ‘갈비탕’도 있어요.
notes.explain_en: 소갈비 is beef ribs and 돼지갈비 is pork ribs. There is also 갈비탕, a ribs soup.

examples.en: I had galbi with my family on the weekend.
We're grilling galbi tonight.
Two servings of galbi here, please.
This galbi is really delicious!
Shall we eat galbi and then have cold noodles, too?

notes.explain: 전화번호는 숫자를 하나씩 읽어요. 0은 보통 ‘공’이라고 해요. 010은 ‘공일공’이에요.
notes.explain_en: Phone numbers are read digit by digit. 0 is usually 공, so 010 is 공일공.

examples.en: I had a meeting, so I couldn't answer the phone.
The office phone keeps ringing.
What is your friend's phone number?
I'm working now. Please call me later.
I got a call from my mom.

notes.explain: 말할 때는 ‘얘기’라고 줄여서 자주 해요. ‘이야기’와 같은 말이에요.
notes.explain_en: In speech people often shorten it to 얘기. It is the same word as 이야기.

examples.en: I laughed a lot when I heard that story.
I listened to my friend's story until late at night.
The story of that movie is really interesting.
The child loves old stories.
Shall we talk for a bit?

notes.explain: ‘귀’는 한 개도 두 개도 ‘귀’예요. 그리고 ‘내 귀’라고 안 해도 돼요. ‘귀가 아파요’만 말해도 ‘내 귀가 아파요’예요.
notes.explain_en: 귀 means one ear or both ears. You also don't need to say 'my': 귀가 아파요 already means 'my ear hurts'.

phrases.example: 제 친구는 귀가 얇아서 광고를 보면 바로 사요.
phrases.meaning_en: Someone who quickly believes or follows what other people say.

phrases.example: 그 말은 귀에 못이 박히게 들었어요.
phrases.literal: “a nail gets stuck in the ear”
phrases.en_equiv: to have heard something a thousand times
phrases.meaning_en: Used when you are tired of hearing the same advice or complaint again and again.

examples.en: I got my ears pierced last year.
My hearing isn't good.

examples.ko: 어제 귀가 아팠어요. 오늘 병원에 갈 거예요.
examples.en: My ear hurt yesterday. I'm going to the hospital today.
It's so noisy. I want to cover my ears.
It's so cold outside. My ears are red.

notes.explain: 샤워는 몸 전체를 씻는 거예요. 얼굴만 씻으면 ‘세수’, 욕조에서 하면 ‘목욕’이라고 해요.
notes.explain_en: 샤워 means washing your whole body. Washing only your face is 세수, and bathing in a tub is 목욕.

examples.en: I shower at night.
You take really long showers.
I exercise and then take a shower.
I'm tired. I want to take a quick shower and sleep.

examples.ko: 샤워는 아침에 해요? — 아니요, 저는 밤에 해요.
examples.en: Do you shower in the morning? — No, I shower at night.

notes.explain: ‘이’는 tooth도, this도, 숫자 2도 될 수 있어요. 소리가 같아서 동사를 보고 뜻을 알아요.
notes.explain_en: 이 can mean tooth, 'this' or the number 2. The sound is the same, so use the verb and the situation to tell which one.

phrases.example: 이를 악물고 끝까지 달렸어요.
phrases.meaning_en: To endure pain or hardship with determination.

examples.en: I brush my teeth after eating.
My tooth hurts, so I'm going to the dentist.
My younger brother lost a tooth.
I had a tooth pulled at the dentist yesterday.
I'll brush my teeth and go to sleep.

notes.explain: 헤어질 때 ‘건강하세요’라고 인사하기도 해요. 어른이나 아픈 분에게 많이 해요.
notes.explain_en: People sometimes say 건강하세요 (stay healthy) as a goodbye, especially to elders or someone who has been sick.

examples.en: Health is the most important thing.
My grandmother's health isn't very good.
I drink a lot of water. It's good for your health.
How is your health these days? — It's very good.
I'm tired these days. I'm worried about my health.

notes.explain: 왼쪽 손은 ‘왼손’, 오른쪽 손은 ‘오른손’이에요. ‘왼’은 left, ‘오른’은 right라는 뜻이에요.
notes.explain_en: The left hand is 왼손 and the right hand is 오른손. 왼 means left and 오른 means right.

phrases.example: 김치는 손이 많이 가는 음식이에요.
phrases.en_equiv: to take a lot of work
phrases.meaning_en: Used for jobs that need a lot of care and effort.

examples.en: I wash my hands when I get home.
My hands are cold in winter.
I had a question. I raised my hand.
I walk with a coffee in one hand.
I walk holding hands with my child.

notes.explain: 눈은 eye도 되고 snow도 돼요: '눈이 와요'는 snow예요. 그리고 '눈치'는 말하지 않아도 분위기를 읽는 힘이에요. 한국 생활에서 아주 중요해요.
notes.explain_en: 눈 means both 'eye' and 'snow': 눈이 와요 means it's snowing. Also, 눈치 is the skill of reading the room without being told — very important in Korean life.

phrases.example: 제 친구는 눈이 너무 높아서 남자 친구가 없어요.
phrases.meaning_en: very picky, especially about dating partners

phrases.example: 방학이 눈 깜짝할 사이에 끝났어요.
phrases.en_equiv: in the blink of an eye
phrases.meaning_en: very quickly

phrases.example: 할머니는 손녀가 눈에 넣어도 아프지 않을 만큼 예쁘대요.
phrases.literal: "wouldn't hurt even if put in the eye"
phrases.en_equiv: close: the apple of one's eye
phrases.meaning_en: loved dearly, usually a child or grandchild

examples.en: The baby has really big eyes.
My older brother has bad eyesight.

examples.ko: 눈이 아파요. 컴퓨터를 너무 오래 봤어요.
examples.en: My eyes hurt. I looked at the computer for too long.
I close my eyes and rest for a moment.
Something got in my eye. Shall I wash it with water?
I open my eyes at seven in the morning.

notes.explain: ‘세수’는 얼굴만 씻는 거예요. ‘세수를 씻어요’라고 하지 않고 ‘세수를 해요’라고 말해요.
notes.explain_en: 세수 means washing only your face. Say 세수를 해요, never 세수를 씻어요.

examples.en: In the morning I just wash my face.
I'll quickly wash my face.
I wash my face and get dressed.
I wash my face with cold water.
Did you wash your face? — Yes, I just did.

notes.explain: 숨 쉬는 코는 ‘코’, 코에서 나오는 물은 ‘콧물’이에요. ‘콧물이 나요’라고 해요. ‘코가 나요’는 이상해요.
notes.explain_en: Your nose is 코 but the liquid from it is 콧물. A runny nose is 콧물이 나요. 코가 나요 sounds wrong.

phrases.example: 학교는 우리 집 코앞이에요.
phrases.meaning_en: Used for places and for time: 시험이 코앞이에요 = 'the exam is right around the corner'.

phrases.example: 그 배우는 코는 예쁜데 콧대가 높아서 인사도 안 해요.
phrases.literal: “the bridge of the nose is high”
phrases.meaning_en: Describes proud, arrogant people who look down on others.

examples.en: I caught a cold, so my nose is blocked.
I breathe through my nose.
My nose is low (flat).
Dogs have a very good sense of smell.
I blew my nose in the restroom.

notes.explain: 옷 이야기에도 ‘팔’을 써요. 반팔은 짧은 소매 옷, 긴팔은 긴 소매 옷이에요. ‘반’은 half라는 뜻이에요.
notes.explain_en: 팔 also appears in clothing words. 반팔 means short sleeves and 긴팔 means long sleeves. 반 means 'half'.

phrases.example: 친구하고 팔짱을 끼고 걸어요.
phrases.en_equiv: to link arms / to fold one's arms
phrases.meaning_en: Two friends walking arm in arm. On your own, it also means crossing your arms over your chest.

phrases.example: 팔은 안으로 굽는다고, 저는 우리 팀을 응원해요.
phrases.meaning_en: A proverb: people naturally take the side of their own family or group.

examples.en: I hurt my arm last week.
My bag is heavy, so my arm hurts.

examples.ko: 팔을 위로 올려요. 그리고 천천히 내려요.
examples.en: Raise your arms up. Then lower them slowly.
I wear my watch on my left arm.
I got a shot in my arm at the hospital.

notes.explain: 발은 발목 아래 부분이에요. 다리(leg)와 달라요. ‘신발’(shoes) 안에도 ‘발’이 들어 있어요.
notes.explain_en: 발 is the part below the ankle. It is not 다리 (leg). The word 신발 (shoes) also contains 발.

phrases.example: 그 친구는 발이 넓어서 모르는 사람이 없어요.
phrases.en_equiv: to know a lot of people
phrases.meaning_en: Someone with a wide network of acquaintances who gets around everywhere.

phrases.example: 이웃이 이사하는 날, 모두 발 벗고 나서서 도왔어요.
phrases.en_equiv: to jump in and help eagerly
phrases.meaning_en: To help with real enthusiasm, without holding back.

examples.en: My dress shoes are small, so my feet hurt.
I wash my feet before going to bed.
My foot size is 270.
My younger brother is a really fast runner.
Someone stepped on my foot on the subway.

notes.explain: 머리는 head도 되고 hair도 돼요. 미용실에서 자르거나 파마하는 걸 그냥 '머리(를) 하다'라고 해요. '머리가 좋다'는 smart라는 뜻이에요.
notes.explain_en: 머리 means both 'head' and 'hair'. Getting your hair cut or permed at the salon is simply 머리(를) 하다. 머리가 좋다 ('good head') means smart.

phrases.example: 우리 같이 머리를 맞대고 생각해 봐요.
phrases.meaning_en: to think about a problem together

phrases.example: 공부하다가 머리 좀 식히러 나왔어요.
phrases.meaning_en: to take a break and relax your mind

phrases.example: 머리에 피도 안 마른 애가 벌써 연애를 해요?
phrases.literal: "blood on the head isn't even dry yet"
phrases.meaning_en: too young and inexperienced

examples.en: My older sister's hair is very long.
I'm washing my hair now.
I have a headache. I want to take some medicine.
I got a haircut yesterday. How does it look?
I take a shower and dry my hair.

notes.explain: ‘일’은 회사 일뿐 아니라 해야 하는 모든 일이에요. ‘일’ 뒤에 ‘-해요’를 붙이면 ‘일해요’(work)가 돼요. 날짜의 ‘일’(5일)과는 달라요.
notes.explain_en: 일 is not only a job. It is anything you have to do. Add 해요 and you get 일해요 (work). It is different from the 일 in dates like 5일.

phrases.example: 급한 일이 생겼어요. 먼저 갈게요.
phrases.meaning_en: A polite way to cancel or leave early without giving details.

examples.en: I have too much work today.
My husband's job is very busy.

examples.ko: 주말에 일이 있어요. 다음 주에 만날까요?
examples.en: I have something to do this weekend. Shall we meet next week?
Let's have dinner together after work.
Is this job difficult? — No, it's easy.

notes.explain: “대학 일 학년”처럼 학년과 같이 말해요. 학교 이름에는 “대학교”가 붙어요: 서울대학교.
notes.explain_en: You say 대학 일 학년 for 'college first year'. A school's official name ends in 대학교, like 서울대학교.
notes.usage: 대학 = college/university. In daily speech 대학교 is more common for the place.

examples.en: I'm starting college next year.
I met a friend from my college days.
I study Korean at college.
My younger sibling is a college freshman.
There are many restaurants in front of the college.

notes.explain: ‘공부를 잘해요’는 성적이 좋다는 뜻이에요. 공부하는 방법이 아니라 결과를 말해요.
notes.explain_en: 공부를 잘해요 means 'is good at school', so it talks about results, not about how someone studies.

examples.en: I study hard.
I study at the library.

examples.ko: 내일 시험이에요. 오늘 공부를 많이 할 거예요.
examples.en: I have an exam tomorrow. I'll study a lot today.
Studying Korean is fun.
Where do you study? — I study at home.

notes.explain: ‘말’은 horse도 되고 ‘words, speech’도 돼요. ‘말을 타요’는 horse, ‘말을 해요’는 speak예요. 동사를 보면 알아요.
notes.explain_en: 말 can be a horse or 'words/speech'. 말을 타요 is about a horse and 말을 해요 means 'speak'. The verb tells you.

phrases.example: 올해는 말띠 해예요.
phrases.en_equiv: born in the Year of the Horse
phrases.meaning_en: One of the twelve zodiac animals. People born every twelve years share it.

examples.en: I rode a horse on Jeju Island.
There are lots of horses on Jeju Island.
The horse eats grass.
That horse is very fast.
I was born in the Year of the Horse. My younger brother was born in the Year of the Dog.

notes.explain: 작고 어린 개는 ‘강아지’라고 해요. 집에서 키우는 개를 귀엽게 부를 때도 ‘강아지’를 많이 써요.
notes.explain_en: A small, young dog is a 강아지 (puppy). People also say 강아지 affectionately for a pet dog of any age.
notes.usage: 개 = dog. Not the same word as the counter 개 (두 개).

phrases.example: 제 친구는 개띠라서 1994년생이에요.
phrases.en_equiv: born in the Year of the Dog
phrases.meaning_en: Koreans often tell their zodiac animal (띠) when they talk about age. Each animal comes back every 12 years.

phrases.example: 하루 종일 자는 우리 개를 보면 개 팔자가 상팔자 같아요.
phrases.literal: “a dog's fate is the best fate”
phrases.en_equiv: it's a dog's life (in the good sense)
phrases.meaning_en: A humorous saying when someone, or a pet, seems to live without any worries.

examples.en: I have a dog.
My dog loves walks.
The dog waits in front of the door.
Do you like dogs? — Yes, I like them a lot.
That dog is very small.

notes.explain: ‘취미로 N을 해요’는 ‘just for fun’이라는 느낌이에요. 직업이 아니라는 뜻도 있어요.
notes.explain_en: 취미로 N을 해요 has a 'just for fun' feel. It also suggests it is not your job.

examples.en: My hobby is cooking.
My husband doesn't have any hobbies.
What's your hobby? — I watch a lot of movies.
I want to find a new hobby.
I'm learning guitar as a hobby.

notes.explain: 식료품은 ‘장을 보다’라고 해요. ‘쇼핑’은 옷이나 신발처럼 구경하면서 살 때 주로 써요.
notes.explain_en: For groceries, Koreans say 장을 보다. 쇼핑 is mostly for things like clothes and shoes, where you look around while you buy.

examples.en: I went shopping with a friend on the weekend.
Shopping is my hobby.
I'm going shopping at the department store tomorrow.
Shall we have coffee together after shopping?
Online shopping is convenient.

notes.explain: ‘연습’은 몸이나 입으로 반복하는 거예요. 노래, 운동, 말하기는 ‘공부’보다 ‘연습’이라고 해요.
notes.explain_en: 연습 is repeating something with your body or mouth. For singing, sports and speaking, Koreans say 연습 rather than 공부.

phrases.example: 연습이 완벽을 만든다고, 매일 말해 봐요.
phrases.meaning_en: A saying used to encourage regular practice.

examples.en: I practice pronunciation every day.
Piano practice is one hour every day.
Practice is important for Korean.

examples.ko: 내일 발표가 있어요. 오늘 연습이 필요해요.
examples.en: I have a presentation tomorrow. I need practice today.
There are lots of practice problems.

notes.explain: 한자로 ‘설’은 ‘말하다’, ‘명’은 ‘밝다’예요. 말해서 환하게 해 주는 거예요.
notes.explain_en: In Chinese characters 설 means 'speak' and 명 means 'bright'. Explaining is speaking to make things clear.

examples.en: That employee's explanation was too hard to follow.
My friend's directions are very detailed.
This word is hard to explain.
The staff member's explanation of the menu is kind and clear.
Is my explanation difficult? — No, it's easy.

notes.explain: ‘시작’의 반대말은 ‘끝’이에요. 동사로는 ‘시작해요’의 반대가 ‘끝나요’(it ends)예요. ‘끝내요’는 ‘I finish it’이에요.
notes.explain_en: The opposite of 시작 is 끝. For verbs, 시작해요 pairs with 끝나요 (it ends), and 끝내요 means 'I finish it'.

examples.en: What time does class start?
We're starting class now.
The movie starts at seven.
I'll start exercising tomorrow.
Hangul is where Korean study starts.

notes.explain: ‘소개해요’는 사람, 가게, 책 모두에 써요. 소개를 받으면 ‘소개받았어요’라고 해요.
notes.explain_en: 소개해요 works for people, shops and books. If someone introduces you to something, say 소개받았어요.

examples.en: Let me introduce myself first.
I came to this place through a friend's recommendation.
I introduced myself in the first class.
This book has a short introduction.
I want to read the company introduction.

notes.explain: 운동화는 ‘운동’ + ‘화’(shoes)예요. 운동할 때뿐 아니라 평소에도 신어요.
notes.explain_en: 운동화 is 운동 + 화 (shoes), meaning sneakers. Koreans wear them for exercise and for everyday life.

examples.en: I work out in the park in the evening.
I don't exercise these days.

examples.ko: 무슨 운동을 좋아해요? — 저는 수영을 좋아해요.
examples.en: What sports do you like? — I like swimming.
I exercise twice a week with a friend.
Let's have lunch together after the workout.

notes.explain: 물건을 제자리에 놓는 건 ‘정리’, 바닥을 닦고 쓰는 건 ‘청소’예요. ‘방 정리’와 ‘방 청소’는 달라요.
notes.explain_en: Putting things back in place is 정리, and sweeping or wiping floors is 청소. 방 정리 and 방 청소 are different jobs.

examples.en: I clean my room on the weekend.

examples.ko: 내일 손님이 와요. 오늘 집 청소가 필요해요.
examples.en: Guests are coming tomorrow. The house needs cleaning today.
Who does the cleaning? — I do.
I clean every Saturday.
Cleaning usually takes thirty minutes.

notes.explain: 수업이나 여행에 필요한 물건은 ‘준비물’이라고 해요. 학교에서 자주 들어요.
notes.explain_en: The things you need to bring for a class or trip are called 준비물. You hear it a lot at school.

phrases.example: 큰 시험이라서 마음의 준비를 했어요.
phrases.meaning_en: Getting yourself ready emotionally for something big or hard.

examples.en: I'm busy preparing for an exam these days.
My husband takes care of dinner preparation.
Is your bag packed? — Yes, shall we go?
I'm preparing for tomorrow's meeting.
Have you finished preparing for the trip?

notes.explain: 사람의 말에는 ‘대답’, 시험 문제에는 ‘답’이라고 해요. 맞는 답은 ‘정답’이에요.
notes.explain_en: For replying to a person use 대답; for a test question use 답. The correct answer is 정답.

examples.en: I called out to my friend, but there's no answer.
It was hard, so I couldn't answer.
The staff member's answers are always kind.
Is my answer right? — Yes, it's right.
Please give me your answer by tomorrow.

notes.explain_en: 배를 타요 is a boat, 배를 먹어요 is a pear, 배가 아파요 is a stomach. The verb tells you which 배 it is.
notes.usage: 배 = stomach (배가 아파요). Also 배 = boat, and 배 = pear.

phrases.en_equiv: to be jealous of a relative's success
phrases.meaning_en: A famous proverb about envy. Said half-jokingly when someone else's luck makes you jealous.

phrases.example: 그 영화를 보고 배꼽이 빠지게 웃었어요.

phrases.meaning_en: To laugh extremely hard.

examples.en: I ate a big lunch, so I'm full.

examples.en: I don't exercise these days. So my belly has grown.

notes.explain: ‘감기에 걸리다’처럼 병 앞에는 ‘에’를 써요. ‘감기를 걸리다’라고 하지 않아요.

notes.explain_en: The place you cross takes 을/를: 길을 건너요. The opposite side is called 건너편.

My Mexican friend lives in Seoul.
Mexico has a really large population.

notes.explain: 예전 이름 “이태리”를 아직도 가끔 들을 수 있어요. 지금 이름은 “이탈리아”예요.
notes.explain_en: You can still sometimes hear the older name 이태리. The current name is 이탈리아.

phrases.example: 이탈리아를 줄여 이태리라고 하고, 목욕탕에서 이태리타월을 써요.
phrases.meaning_en: A rough cloth used to scrub your skin in the bath. The name has Italy in it, but it is an ordinary item in Korean bathhouses.

examples.en: I'm Italian.
I want to go to Italy.
I eat pizza at an Italian restaurant.
My Italian friend loves coffee.
I bought Italian shoes. They are really comfortable.

notes.explain: “인도”는 길 옆의 사람이 걷는 길도 뜻해요. 소리는 같아요. 어느 뜻인지는 앞뒤 말을 보고 알아요.
notes.explain_en: 인도 also means a sidewalk, with exactly the same sound. You tell which one it is from the other words in the sentence.

examples.en: I'm Indian.
I want to go to India.
I eat naan at an Indian restaurant.
India has a huge number of people.
People also use English a lot in India.

notes.explain: 한국어에는 영어의 F 소리가 없어요. 그래서 F를 “ㅍ”으로 써요. 필리핀의 “필”은 Phil이에요. 프랑스의 “프”도 그래요.
notes.explain_en: Korean has no English F sound, so F is written with ㅍ. The 필 in 필리핀 is "Phil", and the 프 in 프랑스 works the same way.

phrases.example: 동생은 필리핀 어학연수를 갔어요.
phrases.en_equiv: English study trip to the Philippines
phrases.meaning_en: A popular way for Korean students to study English abroad for a few months.

examples.en: I'm Filipino.
I want to go to the Philippines.
The sea in the Philippines is really beautiful.
My Filipino friend speaks English well.
Philippine mangoes are very sweet.

notes.explain: 예전에는 “터키”라고 많이 썼어요. 지금은 나라 이름이 “튀르키예”예요. 하지만 사람들은 아직 “터키”라고도 말해요.
notes.explain_en: It used to be written 터키 in Korean. The country's name now is 튀르키예, though many people still say 터키 in daily speech.

examples.en: I'm Turkish.
I want to go to Türkiye (Turkey).
Türkiye is famous for coffee and tea.
My Turkish friend likes Korea.
I'm going on a trip to Türkiye next year.

notes.explain: 이집트에서는 보통 아랍어를 써요. 이집트 친구에게 아랍어 인사를 배워 보면 좋아요.
notes.explain_en: People in Egypt mostly speak Arabic. Learning one Arabic greeting is a nice way to start with an Egyptian friend.

examples.en: I'm Egyptian.
I want to go to Egypt.
There are pyramids in Egypt.
My Egyptian friend watches Korean dramas.
I took a lot of photos in Egypt.

notes.explain: 영어 “land”가 들어간 나라 이름은 “란드”나 “랜드”로 써요. 폴란드, 핀란드는 “란드”이고, 뉴질랜드, 아일랜드는 “랜드”예요.
notes.explain_en: Country names with English "land" end in 란드 or 랜드. 폴란드 and 핀란드 use 란드, while 뉴질랜드 and 아일랜드 use 랜드.

examples.en: I'm Polish.
I want to go to Poland.
Winters in Poland are long and cold.
Polish food includes dumplings.
I took a train in Poland.

notes.explain: 이름이 다섯 글자라서 길어 보여요. “우-크-라-이-나”로 나눠서 읽으면 쉬워요.
notes.explain_en: The name has five syllables, so it looks long. Split it up and it is easy: 우-크-라-이-나.

examples.en: I'm Ukrainian.
I want to go to Ukraine.
My Ukrainian friend studies Korean hard.
Ukraine is famous for wheat.
Among Ukrainian foods, borscht is delicious.

notes.explain: 네덜란드는 자전거가 많은 나라로 유명해요. 이름이 길어서 처음에는 어려워요. “네-덜-란-드”로 천천히 읽어 보세요.
notes.explain_en: The Netherlands is known as a country full of bicycles. The name is long, so read it slowly at first: 네-덜-란-드.

examples.en: I'm Dutch.
I want to go to the Netherlands.
The Netherlands is famous for tulips.
A friend from the Netherlands works in Seoul.
I bought cheese in the Netherlands.

notes.explain: “스웨덴”과 “스위스”는 둘 다 “스”로 시작해서 헷갈려요. 스웨덴은 Sweden, 스위스는 Switzerland예요.
notes.explain_en: 스웨덴 and 스위스 both start with 스, so they are easy to mix up. 스웨덴 is Sweden and 스위스 is Switzerland.

examples.en: I'm Swedish.
I want to go to Sweden.
In Sweden, the nights are long in winter.
There is a Swedish furniture store in Korea too.
I work together with a Swedish friend.

notes.explain: 나라 이름은 소리 나는 대로 써요. “아르헨티나”는 다섯 글자예요. “아-르-헨-티-나”로 나눠서 읽어 보세요.
notes.explain_en: Country names are written as they sound. 아르헨티나 has five syllables. Split it up when you read it: 아-르-헨-티-나.

examples.en: I'm Argentine.
I want to go to Argentina.
Argentina is famous for its beef.
I learned tango in Argentina.

examples.ko: 아르헨티나 친구는 한국 음식을 잘 먹어요.
examples.en: My Argentine friend eats Korean food well.

notes.explain: “콜롬비아”는 나라이고, 미국 대학 이름은 “컬럼비아”예요. 영어로는 비슷하지만 한국어로는 달라요.
notes.explain_en: 콜롬비아 is the country, while the US university is written 컬럼비아. They look alike in English but are spelled differently in Korean.

examples.en: I'm Colombian.
I want to go to Colombia.
Colombia is in the north of South America.
My Colombian friend studies in Seoul.
They speak Spanish in Colombia.

notes.explain: “페루”는 두 글자라서 짧아요. “페-루”라고 또박또박 말해 보세요. “ㅔ” 소리를 분명하게 말하면 돼요.
notes.explain_en: 페루 has only two syllables. Say it clearly: 페-루. Make the ㅔ sound clear.

examples.en: I'm Peruvian.
I want to go to Peru.
I ate ceviche at a Peruvian restaurant.
My Peruvian friend cooks well.
Peru has a lot of mountains.

notes.explain: 고추 같은 “chili”는 “칠리”이고, 나라 이름은 “칠레”예요. 영어로는 소리가 비슷하지만 한국어 글자는 달라요.
notes.explain_en: The spicy "chili" is written 칠리, while the country Chile is 칠레. They sound alike in English, but the Korean spelling differs.

examples.en: I'm Chilean.
I want to go to Chile.
I like Chilean wine.
Chile is very long from top to bottom.
It's summer in Korea. It's winter in Chile.

notes.explain: 이름이 아주 길어서 보통 “사우디”라고 줄여서 말해요. “사우디 사람”, “사우디 여행”처럼 써요.
notes.explain_en: The name is very long, so people usually shorten it to 사우디, as in 사우디 사람 (a Saudi) or 사우디 여행 (a trip to Saudi Arabia).

examples.en: I'm Saudi.
I want to go to Saudi Arabia.
Saudi Arabia is really hot in the daytime.
My friend's older brother works in Saudi Arabia.
Saudi Arabia has a lot of oil.

notes.explain: “이란”과 “이라크”는 이름이 비슷해서 헷갈려요. 둘 다 “이라”로 시작해요. 이란 사람들은 페르시아어를 써요.
notes.explain_en: 이란 (Iran) and 이라크 (Iraq) sound alike because both start with 이라. People in Iran speak Persian (페르시아어).

examples.en: I'm Iranian.
I want to go to Iran.
Iran is next to Türkiye.
Iran is famous for its carpets.
My Iranian friend drinks tea often.

notes.explain: “-스탄”으로 끝나는 나라가 많아요. 파키스탄, 카자흐스탄, 아프가니스탄이 그래요. “스탄”은 “땅, 나라”라는 뜻이에요.
notes.explain_en: Many country names end in -스탄: 파키스탄, 카자흐스탄, 아프가니스탄. 스탄 means "land".

examples.en: I'm Pakistani.
I want to go to Pakistan.
Pakistan is next to India.
My Pakistani friend works at a Korean company.
I had lunch with my Pakistani friend.

notes.explain: 네팔 사람들은 “나마스테”라고 인사해요. 두 손을 모으고 말해요.
notes.explain_en: In Nepal, 나마스테 is a common greeting. People often put their hands together when they say it.

examples.en: I'm Nepali.
I want to go to Nepal.
The mountains in Nepal are really high.

examples.ko: 네팔 식당은 우리 동네에 하나 있어요.
examples.en: There is one Nepali restaurant in our neighborhood.
My Nepali friend often goes to the mountains.

notes.explain: 싱가포르는 도시이면서 나라예요. 끝은 “폴”이 아니라 “포르”로 써요. “싱가폴”은 맞춤법이 틀려요.
notes.explain_en: Singapore is both a city and a country. It ends in 포르, not 폴: the spelling 싱가폴 is wrong.

examples.en: I'm Singaporean.
I want to go to Singapore.
Singapore is a small country.
I met a friend at the airport in Singapore.
I went on a trip to Singapore. The food was delicious.

notes.explain: “홍콩”은 받침 ㅇ이 두 번 나와요. 입을 크게 열고 “홍-콩”이라고 천천히 말해 보세요.
notes.explain_en: 홍콩 has the final consonant ㅇ twice. Open your mouth wide and say it slowly: 홍-콩.

examples.en: I'm from Hong Kong.
I want to go to Hong Kong.
My Hong Kong friend lives in Korea.
The night view of Hong Kong is really beautiful.
The buildings in Hong Kong are very tall.

notes.explain: “대만”과 “태국”은 소리가 비슷해서 헷갈려요. 대만은 Taiwan이고, 태국은 Thailand예요.
notes.explain_en: 대만 and 태국 sound similar and get mixed up. 대만 is Taiwan and 태국 is Thailand.

examples.en: I'm Taiwanese.
I want to go to Taiwan.
I drank milk tea in Taiwan.
Taiwan is close to Korea.
My Taiwanese friend speaks Chinese well.

notes.explain: 카자흐스탄에서는 카자흐어와 러시아어를 같이 써요. 이름이 길어서 “카자흐”라고 줄이기도 해요.
notes.explain_en: In Kazakhstan, people use both Kazakh and Russian. The name is long, so it is sometimes shortened to 카자흐.

phrases.example: 카자흐스탄에는 고려인도 살아요.
phrases.en_equiv: ethnic Koreans of the former Soviet Union
phrases.meaning_en: Koreans who settled in Russia and Central Asia long ago, and their families.

examples.en: I'm Kazakh.
I want to go to Kazakhstan.
Kazakhstan has a huge land area.
My Kazakh friend is learning Korean.
I met many Koreans in Kazakhstan.

notes.explain: 이름이 아주 길어서 “우즈벡”이라고 줄여서 말해요. “우즈벡 사람”, “우즈벡 음식”처럼 써요.
notes.explain_en: The name is very long, so people shorten it to 우즈벡, as in 우즈벡 사람 (an Uzbek) or 우즈벡 음식 (Uzbek food).

examples.en: I'm Uzbek.
I want to go to Uzbekistan.
The bread in Uzbekistan is delicious.
My Uzbek friend attends university.
I saw Samarkand in Uzbekistan.

notes.explain: “나이지리아”와 “니제르”는 이름이 비슷하지만 다른 나라예요. 사람이 아주 많은 큰 나라는 나이지리아예요.
notes.explain_en: 나이지리아 and 니제르 (Niger) have similar names but are different countries. The big country with a huge population is Nigeria.

examples.en: I'm Nigerian.
I want to go to Nigeria.
Nigeria has the most people in Africa.
My Nigerian friend speaks English well.
Nigerian music is popular these days.

notes.explain: “남아공”은 줄임말이에요. 남(남쪽)+아(프리카)+공(화국)이에요. 보통 말할 때와 쓸 때는 줄임말이 더 많이 나와요.
notes.explain_en: 남아공 is a short form: 남 (south) + 아 (from 아프리카, Africa) + 공 (from 공화국, republic). In daily speech and writing the short form is very common.

examples.en: I'm South African.
I want to go to South Africa (short for 남아프리카공화국).
South Africa is in the south of Africa.
My South African friend teaches English in Korea.
The flight from South Africa to Korea is long.

notes.explain: 뉴질랜드의 ‘랜드’는 영어 land예요. 아일랜드도 같아요. 외국 나라 이름은 영어 소리를 한글로 쓴 것이 많아요.
notes.explain_en: The 랜드 in 뉴질랜드 is the English word “land”. 아일랜드 works the same way. Many foreign country names are just English sounds written in Hangul.

examples.en: I'm from New Zealand.
I want to go to New Zealand.
Next year I'm going to live in New Zealand with my family.

examples.ko: 뉴질랜드는 한국에서 멀어요? — 네, 아주 멀어요.
examples.en: Is New Zealand far from Korea? — Yes, very far.

examples.ko: 뉴질랜드 친구하고 다음 주에 점심 먹을 거예요.
examples.en: I'm going to have lunch with my New Zealand friend next week.

notes.explain: 아일랜드(Ireland)와 아이슬란드(Iceland)는 다른 나라예요. 이름이 비슷해서 많이 헷갈려요.
notes.explain_en: 아일랜드 (Ireland) and 아이슬란드 (Iceland) are different countries. The names are close, so people often mix them up.

examples.en: I'm Irish.
I want to go to Ireland.
My friend studied English in Ireland.

examples.ko: 아일랜드는 날씨가 어때요? — 비가 자주 와요.
examples.en: How's the weather in Ireland? — It rains often.

examples.ko: 다음 달에 아일랜드에서 친구하고 만날 거예요.
examples.en: Next month I'm going to meet a friend in Ireland.

notes.explain: 포르투갈 말은 ‘포르투갈어’예요. 브라질에서도 포르투갈어를 써요.
notes.explain_en: The language of Portugal is 포르투갈어. People in Brazil speak Portuguese too.

examples.en: I'm Portuguese.
I want to go to Portugal.
This summer I'm going to swim in the sea in Portugal.
I talked with a Portuguese person in English.
Shall we meet at a Portuguese restaurant this weekend?

notes.explain: 나라 이름 뒤에 ‘어’를 붙이면 그 나라 말이 될 때가 많아요. 그리스어는 Greek이에요. 일본어, 중국어도 같아요.
notes.explain_en: Add 어 after a country name and you often get its language: 그리스어 is Greek. 일본어 and 중국어 work the same way.

examples.en: I'm Greek.
I want to go to Greece.
I ordered a salad at a Greek restaurant.
I study Korean together with a Greek friend.
Greece is very hot in summer.

notes.explain: 스위스에는 ‘스위스어’가 없어요. 독일어, 프랑스어, 이탈리아어 같은 말을 써요.
notes.explain_en: There is no language called “Swiss”. People in Switzerland speak German, French, Italian and others.

examples.en: I'm Swiss.
I want to go to Switzerland.

examples.ko: 스위스에서 산을 보고 사진을 많이 찍었어요.
examples.en: In Switzerland I looked at the mountains and took lots of photos.
In Switzerland I took a train to a lake.
I rested for two days with a friend at a hotel in Switzerland.

notes.explain: 오스트리아(Austria)와 오스트레일리아(Australia)는 달라요. 오스트레일리아는 보통 ‘호주’라고 해요.
notes.explain_en: 오스트리아 (Austria) and 오스트레일리아 (Australia) are different. Australia is usually just called 호주.

phrases.example: 오스트리아의 도시 이름이 들어간 비엔나소시지를 먹어요.
phrases.meaning_en: Small, thin sausages that are a classic side dish in Korean lunch boxes. Koreans call the city of Vienna 빈 or 비엔나.

examples.en: I'm Austrian.
I want to go to Austria.
I went to a concert in Austria.
What's the capital of Austria? — It's Vienna.

examples.ko: 겨울에 친구하고 오스트리아에서 스키를 탈 거예요.
examples.en: This winter I'm going to ski in Austria with a friend.

notes.explain: ‘사우나’라는 말은 핀란드 말에서 왔어요. 핀란드 사람들에게 사우나는 아주 가까운 문화예요.
notes.explain_en: The word “sauna” comes from Finnish. Saunas are a very familiar part of life in Finland.

examples.en: I'm Finnish.
I want to go to Finland.
Finland is very cold in winter.
My Finnish friend came to Seoul last week.
I waited for an hour at the airport in Finland.

notes.explain: ‘산’은 ‘그 나라에서 나온 것’이라는 뜻이에요. 마트에서 ‘노르웨이산 연어’를 자주 볼 수 있어요.
notes.explain_en: 산 after a place name means “produced there”. In supermarkets you often see 노르웨이산 연어, Norwegian salmon.

examples.en: I'm Norwegian.
I want to go to Norway.
In Norway the nights are long in winter.
My Norwegian friend likes kimchi.
What shall we do in Norway? — Shall we take a boat?

notes.explain: 영어 Danish는 덴마크 사람, 덴마크 말, 덴마크 빵을 모두 말해요. 한국어에서 ‘데니시’는 보통 빵이에요.
notes.explain_en: The English word “Danish” covers Danish people, the language and the pastry. In Korean, 데니시 usually means the pastry.

phrases.example: 덴마크 쿠키 통을 열었는데 반짇고리가 있었어요.
phrases.en_equiv: Danish butter cookies (in the blue tin)
phrases.meaning_en: The blue tin of butter cookies is a common gift in Korea. Many families reuse the empty tin as a sewing box (반짇고리), so opening one can be a funny surprise.

examples.en: I'm Danish.
I want to go to Denmark.
My Danish friend studies Korean in Seoul.
I have a meeting in Denmark next week.
In Denmark people ride bicycles a lot.

notes.explain: 벨기에는 ‘기에’로 써요. ‘기애’가 아니에요. ‘에’와 ‘애’를 조심하세요.
notes.explain_en: Write it 벨기에, ending in 에, not 애. Be careful with 에 and 애; they sound alike.

examples.en: I'm Belgian.
I want to go to Belgium.
I ate waffles in Belgium.
From Belgium I go to France by train.
I had lunch with my Belgian friend.

notes.explain: 체코의 수도 이름은 ‘프라하’예요. 영어 Prague와 소리가 달라서 처음에는 헷갈려요.
notes.explain_en: The capital of Czechia is 프라하. It sounds quite different from English “Prague”, so it can be confusing at first.

phrases.example: 체코 프라하에서 찍은 드라마가 '프라하의 연인'이에요.
phrases.meaning_en: A well-known Korean TV drama that was filmed in Prague. Many Koreans think of the city when they hear this title.

examples.en: I'm Czech.
I want to go to Czechia.
I want to study abroad in Czechia.
I went to a Christmas market in Czechia.
Shall we meet my Czech friend at a Korean restaurant?

notes.explain: 헝가리 사람의 이름은 한국처럼 성이 먼저 와요. 유럽에서는 조금 드문 순서예요.
notes.explain_en: In Hungary the family name comes first, just like in Korea. That is a rare order in Europe.

examples.en: I'm Hungarian.
I want to go to Hungary.
I lived in Hungary for a year.
Hungarian dishes have a lot of paprika.
My Hungarian friend's wedding is on Saturday.

notes.explain: ‘이스라엘어’라는 말은 없어요. 많은 사람이 쓰는 말은 ‘히브리어’예요. 나라 이름 + 어 규칙과 달라요.
notes.explain_en: There is no language called 이스라엘어. A language many people use there is 히브리어 (Hebrew). It does not follow the country name + 어 pattern.

examples.en: I'm Israeli.
I want to go to Israel.
I met my Israeli friend in the park.
Israel is really hot in summer.
Next year I'm going to study in Israel.

notes.explain: 이름이 길어서 ‘UAE’라고도 해요. 한국어로는 ‘유에이이’라고 읽어요.
notes.explain_en: The name is long, so people also write UAE. In Korean it is read as 유에이이.

examples.en: I'm Emirati.
I want to go to the United Arab Emirates.
I have a meeting with a company from the UAE.
It's ten hours by plane to the UAE.
My friend from the UAE likes Korean food.

notes.explain: ‘방글라’는 벵골 말이고 ‘데시’는 ‘나라’라는 뜻이에요. 방글라데시는 ‘벵골 사람들의 나라’예요.
notes.explain_en: 방글라 means Bengali and 데시 means “country”. So 방글라데시 is “the country of the Bengali people”.

examples.en: I'm Bangladeshi.
I want to go to Bangladesh.
My Bangladeshi friend works at a company in Seoul.
I have family in Bangladesh.
During vacation I'm going to meet a friend in Bangladesh.

notes.explain: 스리랑카 사람들은 ‘싱할라어’와 ‘타밀어’를 많이 써요. ‘스리랑카어’라는 말은 쓰지 않아요.
notes.explain_en: People in Sri Lanka mainly speak Sinhala and Tamil. There is no language called “Sri Lankan”.

examples.en: I'm Sri Lankan.
I want to go to Sri Lanka.
I drank black tea in Sri Lanka.
I had curry with my Sri Lankan friend.
In Sri Lanka I took a train to a tea field.

notes.explain: 나라 이름 뒤에 ‘사람’을 붙이면 그 나라 사람이에요. 미얀마 사람, 한국 사람처럼요.
notes.explain_en: Add 사람 after a country name to say a person from that country: 미얀마 사람, 한국 사람.

examples.en: I'm from Myanmar.
I want to go to Myanmar.
My Myanmar friend works in Seoul.

examples.ko: 미얀마는 지금 몇 시예요? — 여섯 시예요.
examples.en: What time is it in Myanmar now? — It's six o'clock.

examples.ko: 내년에 미얀마에 갈 거예요. 친구가 거기에 살아요.
examples.en: I'm going to Myanmar next year. A friend lives there.

notes.explain: 캄보디아 말은 ‘크메르어’예요. ‘캄보디아어’보다 ‘크메르어’라는 이름을 더 많이 써요.
notes.explain_en: The language of Cambodia is called 크메르어 (Khmer). That name is used more often than “캄보디아어”.

examples.en: I'm Cambodian.
I want to go to Cambodia.
I looked around a temple in Cambodia.
My Cambodian friend likes Korean songs.
Cambodia is hot all year round.

notes.explain: 라오스는 바다가 없는 나라예요. 이런 나라를 ‘내륙국’이라고도 해요.
notes.explain_en: Laos has no sea. A country like that is also called 내륙국 (a landlocked country).

examples.en: I'm Lao.
I want to go to Laos.
I bought coffee in Laos.
During summer vacation I met a friend in Laos.
Shall we eat rice noodles at a Lao restaurant?

notes.explain: 쿠바는 카리브해에 있는 섬나라예요. ‘섬’은 바다 가운데에 있는 땅이에요.
notes.explain_en: Cuba is an island country in the Caribbean Sea. 섬 means “island”.

examples.en: I'm Cuban.
I want to go to Cuba.
I want to learn Spanish in Cuba.

examples.ko: 쿠바 음악 좋아해요? — 네, 아주 좋아해요.
examples.en: Do you like Cuban music? — Yes, I like it a lot.

examples.ko: 내년에 친구하고 쿠바에서 한 달 있을 거예요.
examples.en: Next year I'm going to stay in Cuba for a month with a friend.

notes.explain: 모로코는 아프리카 북쪽에 있는 나라예요. 지도에서 스페인 아래쪽을 보세요.
notes.explain_en: Morocco is in the north of Africa. On a map, look just below Spain.

examples.en: I'm Moroccan.
I want to go to Morocco.
I looked around the markets in Morocco.
Morocco is very far from Korea.
Shall we have lunch at a Moroccan restaurant?

notes.explain: 카페 메뉴에서 ‘케냐’라는 이름을 볼 수 있어요. 커피 원두 이름으로 쓰는 경우가 많아요.
notes.explain_en: You may see 케냐 on a café menu. It is often used as the name of a coffee bean.

examples.en: I'm Kenyan.
I want to go to Kenya.
One cup of Kenyan coffee, please.
Kenya is in the east of Africa.
My Kenyan friend goes to a university in Seoul.

notes.explain: ‘드라큘라’ 이야기의 배경은 루마니아의 지역이에요. 그래서 한국 책이나 영화에서 루마니아 이름이 나와요.
notes.explain_en: The story of Dracula is set in a region of Romania, so the country's name shows up in Korean books and films about it.

examples.en: I'm Romanian.
I want to go to Romania.
I work together with a Romanian friend.
Romania has a lot of mountains.
Shall we meet my Romanian friend at the market?
